rules_evaluated.evidence: Pre-existing, unchanged by this pin's diff. Two clauses fail the rule's 2026-08-23 predicate-leak addendum ('Any clause promising what a later beat will do is cartography however the sentence starts... State the present fact; let the later module do its own work'). (1) Line 71, subject test: 'Module 4 reads this skill as part of the system you have: it walks a real task against everything you've built, and the test-strategy skill is the quality-criterion anchor in that walk.' Subject is 'Module 4' (a training component), predicate promises what Module 4's own body will do -- exactly the failure mode `compounded/2026-08-23-student_facing-later-module-predicate-is-still-cartography.md` targets. The section '## What this sets up' is not on the rule's exempt-section list (`## What You'll Learn`, `## Connections`, `## Bridge`/`## Next`, `## Prework`, `**The point:**`), so it does not inherit their exemption. Deletion test: cutting the clause and reading the Note paragraph directly after the header loses nothing a student needs today. (2) Line 67, trailing clause of the What-happened block: 'The module's close sharpens it from what the invocation showed.' The block already completes check_writing.md §16's three-move shape at 'Shipped.'; this is a fourth, unlicensed clause whose subject ('The module's close') and predicate both name a later beat's job. Deletion test: 'Shipped.' reads complete on its own against the following '## What this sets up' section, which already carries the Module-4 forward-pointer. Checked the maintainer block for a dated accept-note covering either passage -- none found (the four accept-notes present concern the Lean-pass cut list, install-mechanic canonicalization, the Emphasis pass, and the Quality stamp; none addresses lines 67 or 71). Harm: cartography with a friendlier face -- both clauses bind this file to a shape a later beat (M3's own close, or M4's module file) may not take, and go stale silently if that beat's design changes without anyone re-reading this exercise. Not blocking per the writing-class template's blocking list (§33 is a check_student_facing judgment rule, not one of the six named hard-grep/creator-name/value-prop categories).

rules_evaluated.evidence: No self-consistency/majority-vote/ensemble method in either prompt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Markdown shout (`**bold**`, `*italic*`) inside fenced prompts = dead weight in Claude Code.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt's fenced body (expanded view) contains bold/italic markdown; both use plain sentences and backtick code spans only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Runtime-fork prompts: paired divs, shared chip.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fires only on Agents 101 / future dual-runtime; AE101 is Code-only and ignores this pattern per the rule's own text.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Runtime-mechanical scaffolding asymmetry — MORE in less-fluent fork, not less.
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 Code-only; no Cowork fork exists to check.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Append-vs-integrate — name integration mode on regeneration with new context source.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No regeneration-with-new-context-source scenario in either prompt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Citation discipline — extend cite-or-flag scope + quote supporting sentence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt asks Claude to cite sources.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Niceness tax — name the edge or pin the line on regeneration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No anti-positioning/edge-carrying regeneration scenario.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Question-dump default — `in turn` too soft; two legal shapes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1 (expanded): 'Use the AskUserQuestion tool to interview me: one question per tool call, wait for my answer, then the next.' -- structural shape (a), the stronger of the two legal forms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Overwrite anxiety — name overwrite default on regeneration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1 writes `~/.claude/skills/test-strategy/SKILL.md` as a first-time create at a known, unambiguous path; not a regeneration-of-existing-file scenario.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action — design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt has 4+ named sub-steps or invokes plan mode; no structural trigger for a preamble suppressor.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-critique register, not defense, when Claude interrogates own work.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 2: 'is it good? Does it reflect how testing actually works on this codebase, or does it read generic?' and body line 48 ('ask the skill itself to name its own weakest part... don't settle for reassurance') both use self-critique framing, not defense-verb framing (no 'defend', 'justify', 'prove').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Minimal hand-off + Claude self-augments for send-off prompts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt is a long-running walk-away send-off; both run inside the same short conversation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Grill before save — collaborative quality at artefact assembly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1 ends 'Show me before saving' rather than a grill-me close. Judged PASS because the exercise substitutes a stronger mechanism for the harm rule 20 guards against (gaps surfacing after the student has walked away): the Sharpen section (line 48, after Phase 2's real invocation against the actual codebase) is a harsher, evidence-based critique than a pre-save grill could be, and it happens within the same 20-minute session with the student still present -- the walked-away-gap scenario this rule protects against does not arise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1's 'Show me before saving' matches check_student_facing.md §6's canonical ask+destination close, not this rule's target (post-comment/send-email/commit-code/push-branch side effects). Writing a personal skill file locally, with the student present, is not the external/side-effect action class this rule addresses.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompt-body edits require maintainer approval — registry files AND inline blocks.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This pin's diff makes no edit to either prompt registry file's body; the gate is not triggered.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact destinations are explicit subpaths, never naked filenames (Agents 101-specific).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule scoped to Agents 101's training-imposed subfolder structure; this is an AE101 exercise using the student's own repo.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 2 ('on this codebase and repository, on the code as it stands in this worktree') references the current worktree by name, not an absolute CWD path or a `cd` command.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `subagent` allowed in prompt blocks; explain why after prompt.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt mentions `subagent`.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Maintainer-approval edits — ONE-AT-A-TIME, PRIORITY-ORDERED, FOUR-FIELD cards.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Process rule for how the orchestrator surfaces edits; not a content property of this file. No prompt-body edit occurred this pin.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name consumer at write time — `Save it as <path>` requires downstream reader.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1 writes `~/.claude/skills/test-strategy/SKILL.md`; the consumer is named in body context (line 22: 'auto-discovered in every session you run, across every repo', and Phase 2 explicitly invokes it) -- category (a), another session/invocation reads it, not a student-only write.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strong-bold prompt label is exactly `**Prompt**` — custom labels break renderer.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Expanded view confirms `**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*` exactly, for both prompts; no custom label text.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Normal work request before orchestration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1 opens 'I want to author a test-strategy skill for this codebase' -- a direct natural request matching what a student would really ask at work, not an 'Ask me which files...' orchestration wrapper.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-test corrections preserve operator workflow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Not a live-test-correction scenario.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File uses `{{prompt:author-test-strategy-skill-1}}` and `{{prompt:author-test-strategy-skill-2}}` markers (lines 27, 44), each preceded by its lead-in sentence; no inline fenced prompt block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Module names in prompt prose are fine — they ground the session.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No module names appear inside either prompt fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Git-output greps asserting exact-N need multi-result fallback.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt text-greps git output.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 2 read in isolation: 'this worktree' resolves from the session's actual cwd regardless of body context, and skill invocation is by name (auto-discovered), so the fence is self-sufficient without needing body callouts to bind it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Repeated Q&A → premature re-edits. Separate iteration from persistence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1's AskUserQuestion loop does not write to SKILL.md per-turn; the write happens once, at the end ('When you have enough, write...'), so the premature-mid-dialog-rewrite failure mode this rule targets cannot occur.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1 has 4 paragraphs, each a distinct move (ask / cover-at-minimum / interview mechanics / write-and-show); Prompt 2 has 2 paragraphs (invoke / self-grade). Both read-aloud cleanly at paragraph boundaries.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Orient saved rule by where it FIRES, not surface activity producing it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Not a save-a-rule-to-CLAUDE.md prompt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1 lead-in ('Ask Claude to author the skill...') shares verb+noun with the prompt's opening ('I want to author a test-strategy skill...'). Prompt 2 lead-in ('Ask Claude to invoke the skill on this codebase and grade what it produced...') shares verb+noun+location with the prompt's opening ('Invoke the `test-strategy` skill on this codebase...').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Declare `permission-mode:` when paste requires specific Claude Code mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt's behavior depends on a specific permission mode; default mode applies.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 2 does not rely on scrollback continuity from prompt 1 even if the session were cold: skill invocation is disk-based (auto-discovered by name), so the prompt is self-sufficient regardless of session-boundary state.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Concurrent-worktree corollary.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 2 explicitly anchors to 'this worktree' ('on the code as it stands in this worktree'), matching the corollary exactly; the backing-block source note for `cc-skills-user-scope` names this exact concern (skill crosses worktrees, its inputs do not) as the design's load-bearing platform claim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Warm ≠ referent-present.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt uses a curriculum-coined definite-article event label (e.g. 'the second-pass read'); both name concrete, in-scope objects (the codebase, the skill, the strategy).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-vs-STOP tail ordering — last imperative wins.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1's write imperative ('When you have enough, write `~/.claude/skills/test-strategy/SKILL.md`...') is followed only by 'Show me before saving' -- no STOP that follows and blocks the write.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headless-runner discipline — tail every prompt with no-AUQ guard.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is an interactive student-run exercise in Claude Code, not a headless/tmux-runner/CI scenario; prompt 1 in fact wants AskUserQuestion to fire.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Long-running prompts stream progress — never go silent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither prompt runs more than a couple of minutes; not a cross-project scan or walk-away send-off.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A leading-looking line can be a forcing function; prefer the simpler prompt.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Editorial guard for fix passes on existing prompts; neither prompt was edited this pin.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompt paths match Builder scope.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule text is scoped to Agents 101's two-scope training-dir convention; this is an AE101 exercise using the student's own repo (no training-imposed subfolder structure).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Output shape — trust Claude's defaults, don't pad.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 1 specifies shape only where the teaching moment depends on it ('frontmatter with name + description, then instructions' -- the SKILL.md format itself), then ends with destination + 'Show me before saving'; no padded trailing shape spec beyond that.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: "Add X and regenerate" is a trap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No append-vs-integrate regeneration scenario in either prompt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Vary closings deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Corpus-wide closing-mechanic variety cannot be assessed from a single file; this exercise's own close (solo self-critique with Claude, line 48, plus real-invocation grading) is a defensible, non-default choice for its module, but scoring variety across the training is out of this single-file judge's scope.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: (Whole-compendium scope call, not a numbered-rule verdict)
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a student-facing curriculum exercise, not buyer-facing copy (site, newsletter, sponsor deck, pricing) -- check_sales_copy.md does not govern this surface.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: (Whole-compendium scope call, not a numbered-rule verdict)

This is an exercise file with none of those sections; its only mood reference ('Mood target: earned trust, culminating') lives in the maintainer Meta block, not body, and is addressed under check_student_facing.md §37 above rather than independently re-verified against the strategy doc by this class.
